description: Align Server ownership boundaries by removing dead workspace execution, enforcing module dependencies, and colocating durable domain reactions without breaking dead-letter redelivery.

tasks.title: Remove Server-local workspace execution
tasks.description: Remove the unused `IGitService` and `GitService` execution surface, its DI registration, runner-root helper, fake, and fixture overrides. Preserve the existing `IRunnerWorkspaceClient` path so all workspace reads and removal continue to be delegated to the assigned runner.
acceptanceCriteria: Production and test code contain no `IGitService`, `GitService`, or `FakeGitService` references.
Workspace route coverage continues to prove requests are forwarded through `IRunnerWorkspaceClient`.
The Server builds and the affected workspace API/spec tests pass.
tasks.output: Server has no local git/workspace execution registration or test fake; workspace APIs remain runner-backed.
tasks.notes: Do not replace the deleted service with another Server-local adapter.

tasks.title: Codify Server ownership and Epic dependency rules
tasks.description: Document daemon self-management and runner failure classifications as facts in `design/architecture.md`. Extend the architecture dependency matrix to include Epic while explicitly permitting only the observed Issue/Epic same-context directions.
acceptanceCriteria: The architecture table scopes Server process execution to Mohist daemon self-management and excludes user-project execution.
The facts-and-decisions section states that retry classifications are runner facts and Workflow is the retry decision authority.
Architecture tests include Epic, permit the existing Issue/Epic collaboration directions, and fail for an unapproved Epic dependency.
Mohist.Server.ArchTests pass.
tasks.output: Architecture documentation and dependency guards consistently encode Server, Runner, Workflow, Issue, and Epic ownership.

tasks.title: Stabilize durable handler identities
tasks.description: Extend subscription registration and dispatch to use an optional explicit handler identity instead of always deriving one from the runtime full type name. Preserve the old `Mohist.Server.Events.Subscriptions.*` identities for every handler that will move, so historical and newly created dead letters resolve after namespace relocation.
acceptanceCriteria: A subscription without an explicit identity retains the current full-type-name identity.
A relocated handler can declare its pre-relocation full name as its durable identity.
A dead-letter row recorded with a moved handler's pre-relocation identity is redelivered to the relocated handler.
Event dispatcher unit tests, including the legacy-identity redelivery regression, pass.
tasks.output: Durable subscription identity is explicit where needed and remains stable across namespace relocation.
tasks.notes: Keep the `FailingHandler` storage schema unchanged; compatibility is encoded in the subscription identity.

tasks.title: Colocate Issue and Epic lifecycle reactions
tasks.description: Move Issue workflow start, workflow completion, epic-change, and composite handlers plus `ParentCompositeRecomputeDispatcher` into Issue. Move all Epic auto-progress handlers plus `EpicProgressRecomputeDispatcher` and `EpicEventRecomputeDispatcher` into Epic, assigning each its legacy durable identity from T-003.
acceptanceCriteria: `IssueWorkflowStartHandler`, `IssueWorkflowCompletionHandler`, `IssueEpicChangedHandler`, every `IssueComposite*Handler`, and `ParentCompositeRecomputeDispatcher` reside in Issue.
Every `Epic*Handler`, `EpicProgressRecomputeDispatcher`, and `EpicEventRecomputeDispatcher` resides in Epic.
Existing Issue and Epic handler tests continue to verify subscriptions, recomputation, workflow context refresh, idempotent behavior, and dispatcher failure handling.
The affected Server spec tests pass.
tasks.output: Issue and Epic lifecycle reactions are discoverable with their owning domains and retain their durable event behavior.
tasks.notes: Keep CloudEvent contracts and assembly scanning unchanged.

tasks.title: Colocate Workflow and Runner lifecycle reactions
tasks.description: Move `WorkflowStageLockReleaseHandler` into Workflow and `RunnerWorkflowTerminalStatusHandler` into Runner, each with its legacy durable identity. Retain current subscription patterns, awaited dispatch failures, and runner cleanup eligibility semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Workflow stage-completed and stage-failed events still release the corresponding stage lock through durable dispatch.
Completed and stopped workflow runs still notify the owning runner, while failed runs remain cleanup-ineligible.
Both handlers reside in their assigned feature modules and retain their pre-relocation durable identities.
Focused stage-lock and runner terminal-status unit/spec tests pass after explicit test registrations and imports are updated.
tasks.output: Workflow and Runner lifecycle reactions reside with their owning modules without changing workspace cleanup behavior.
tasks.notes: Do not move runner filesystem operations into Server.

tasks.title: Colocate Agent routing reactions
tasks.description: Move `RoutingDispatchHandler`, `MentionDispatchHandler`, `RoutedAgentLaunchContextResolver`, `ResponsePromptRenderer`, and `MentionTokenParser` into Agent, preserving the two handlers' legacy durable identities. Preserve wildcard routing, envelope-only evaluation, self-response protection, mention loop prevention, and Agent launch behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The Agent routing and mention handlers and their listed helpers reside in Agent and remain assembly-discovered exactly once.
Routing behavior continues to preserve event lineage, inactive-agent handling, watch behavior, self-response suppression, and mention loop prevention.
The moved handlers retain their pre-relocation durable identities.
Routing and mention unit/spec coverage passes, including service-graph registration assertions.
tasks.output: Agent event routing is colocated with Agent state and launch behavior while retaining existing delivery semantics.
tasks.notes: Do not broaden routing rule semantics or alter event payloads.

tasks.title: Colocate notification reactions and verify boundary alignment
tasks.description: Move `InboxProjectionHandler` into Inbox and `HermesIssueNotificationHandler` into Notifications with their legacy durable identities. Preserve Inbox durable projection behavior and Hermes asynchronous best-effort delivery, then add the source-level inventory assertion and run the issue's complete verification suite.
acceptanceCriteria: `InboxProjectionHandler` resides in Inbox and retains durable dispatcher retry/dead-letter behavior for projection failures.

`HermesIssueNotificationHandler` resides in Notifications and preserves asynchronous best-effort delivery: post-enqueue failures are logged and do not enter CloudEvent dispatcher retry or dead-letter handling.
Every handler and helper in the design inventory resides in its assigned feature module, and `Events/Subscriptions` contains no domain subscription handler.
All moved handlers retain their pre-relocation durable identities and service-graph registration coverage passes.
`npm test`, `npm run typecheck -w packages/web`, and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: Inbox and Notifications reactions are colocated with their owners, and the complete Server/Web verification suite proves the aligned plan.
tasks.notes: Keep generic event dispatch, persistence, and CloudEvent contracts in Infrastructure.
